From: Alex Ramos <alex.ramos@parcelsense.io>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 4 Sep 2026 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: Quick demo request — thinking about inference for routing

Hi Jordan,

I signed up on your self-serve flow yesterday and poked around the API. We run real-time routing for last-mile deliveries and are evaluating inference runtimes to replace an on-prem transformer stack. I wanted a short demo to understand latency characteristics, batching behavior, and how caching might help with repeated addresses.

High-level details:
- Use case: address normalization + intent classification + routing priority (single-turn requests)
- Expected daily volume: ~25M requests/month (mostly short, <= 64 tokens)
- Concurrency: peaks ~650 RPS for 2–3 hour windows, baseline ~120 RPS
- Timeline: pilot within 3 weeks, production Q1 2027

I attached a quick traffic snapshot (CSV) — happy to share SSO/space details in demo. Do you have a 30-minute slot next week? We're PST.

Thanks,
Alex Ramos
Head of Platform Integrations
Parcelsense

Attachment: parcelsense_traffic_snapshot.csv (CSV, 28KB)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Ramos <alex.ramos@parcelsense.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 4 Sep 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick demo request — use case & expected throughput

Hi Alex — great to meet you and thanks for the details + traffic snapshot. Short answers up front: Redwood can handle bursts like that with Dedicated pools + smart routing; KV prefix caching will likely cut token counts on repeat addresses.

Before we lock a slot, a couple quick qualification questions so the demo is targeted: 
1) Are the 25M/mo requests authenticated API calls (one tokenized prompt per request) or are some of these batched server-side now?
2) What percent of requests include user-provided text vs structured address fields (i.e., free-text address lines)?
3) Are you planning to use embeddings for retrieval/nearest-neighbor (we can cover embedding throughput separately)?
4) Any regulatory constraints (on-prem/VPC) for the pilot, or is hosted API acceptable for the demo?

Proposed 30-min windows (PST):
- Tue 9/8 10:00–10:30
- Wed 9/9 14:00–14:30
- Thu 9/10 09:00–09:30

If none of those work, I'm happy to share a Calendly link. I'll include Ben (SDR) on the call so we can follow up on POC steps and a mutual action plan.

Cheers,
Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
redwood.ai

Attachment: redwood-demo-agenda.pdf (PDF, 12KB)

From: Alex Ramos <alex.ramos@parcelsense.io>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 4 Sep 2026 10:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick demo request — use case & expected throughput

Thanks Jordan — answers inline below.

> 1) Are the 25M/mo requests authenticated API calls or batched server-side?
Most are authenticated API calls from our edge fleet. We do a tiny amount of server-side aggregation (~5% of volume) but plan to keep requests single-call through the pilot.

> 2) Percent free-text vs structured?
Roughly 65% free-text address lines (customers typing), 35% structured.

> 3) Embeddings?
We use a small, local NN for geohash lookup today; probably won't use embeddings in the first pilot — focus is on generation/classification latency and deterministic outputs.

> 4) Hosted OK?
Hosted API is fine for the pilot. For production we may evaluate Dedicated or Private depending on SLAs.

Any chance we can do Tue 9/8 at 10:00 PST — that works for our ops lead and me. If it helps, please send an invite to ops@parcelsense.io.

Alex
